items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I played a big festival in Birmingham with the Milliner-Littlejohn sextet and Ben Webster. ... In September, I was engaged for a concert in Antwerp with Ben Webster, Buddy Tate, Jimmy Woody, Wallace Bishop, Milt Buckner and Joe Turner. It was nice to blow with those guys who were all friends.

ctx.x: We arrived in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, the next day. Our cousin Andre Hoffmann and his wife Denise met us and we drove to Sunbury where we spent the night and the next day, visiting the country. Left Sunbury via Harrisburg for New York which was a three hour trip with the train and had the same suite in the Hotel Schluyler that we occupied before going to Cincinnati. George, again, didn't want us to pay anything. We met his mother, Ismay, and we invited her to come to Europe for the summer. Lily offered her to…

We made the rounds of different clubs, were invited to parties and dinners, including one that Herb Flemming prepared for us in his Bronx home. We also caught Ben Webster on his opening night at the Village Vanguard. Ben had a fine trio backing him, but the only musician I can remember was Philly Jo Jones whom I had never met before. Later that night, Tony Scott came in and blew some baritone sax and had a gone jam session with Ben who was playing his can-off that night.

Saturday nights there was always a session at Central Plaza on East 3rd street which was run by Jack Crystal who at one time managed the sessions for Milt Gabler at Jimmie Rhyan on 52nd street. Jack was a real friend to all jazz musicians regardless of race or religion and his sessions were often a big help to many of the fellows that played them.
